title: 1996 AHSME Problem 14
statement: Let \(E(n)\) denote the sum of the even digits of \(n.\) For example, \(E(5681)=6+8=14.\) Find \[ \begin{gathered} E(1)+E(2)+E(3)+\cdots\\ {}+E(100). \end{gathered} \]

solutions.text: From \(00\) through \(99,\) each digit occurs \(10\) times in each of the two positions. The positive even digits sum to \(2+4+6+8=20,\) so the total contribution is \(2\cdot10\cdot20=400.\) The number \(100\) contributes no even positive digit, so the correct answer is C.
hints: Include leading zeros and consider the integers from \(00\) through \(99\)
In each digit position, every digit occurs equally often
